$comment: One authority per concern, written down because it cannot be trusted.
Prime Agent, like the upstream Pi it descends from, resolves competing
extension handlers silently by load order, and exposes no runtime API for
enumerating loaded extensions. A second owner is therefore an undetectable
failure mode, and this file is the only place it can be caught. With Issue
#17 the Governor also owns durable state of its own (a session registry and
a mutation ledger) whose single-writer claims live here too.
`concerns` is an ARRAY, not an object keyed by concern: an object cannot
represent two owners for one key, which would make the duplicate check
vacuous. The check has to be able to fail.
`status: "unassigned"` is a real entry, not a placeholder to be tidied
away. Naming an unowned concern is what stops it being quietly adopted by

concerns.note: The pinned Prime Agent release. Supervisor, resident and client-owned workers, session leases, command journals, schedules, RLM children, sessions and ACP are ADOPTED from the substrate and not reimplemented (ADR 0009 §3).
Prime's own session JSONL. Command Governor ships no competing transcript format; the Governor's durable records are a separate concern with a separate owner.

Refuses to speak to a daemon whose daemon_hello does not match pins.json (protocol name/version, appVersion, schemaRevision) before any command can be sent. governor/prime/substrate.ts is the sole reader of pins.json at runtime; the client consumes it.
The positive allowlist applied on both edges: the supervisor spawn environment and the wire launchEnv. Nothing else may assemble an environment for Prime.
D8. Defines canonical and fences it to the configured session directory. There is no default path and no fallback; omission fails preflight.

D1. Logical identity is Prime's stable sessionId; active-session ids are incarnations. Holds the stale-incarnation fence and the recovery lease. Extension-owned durable sidecar, never the session JSONL.
D1. The one reopen loop: detect workerState=failed (never activity), take the lease, create on the same canonical path exactly once, bind the new incarnation, refuse a sessionId mismatch.

D2. The only decision procedure that may turn a daemon response into COMPLETED/FAILED/UNCERTAIN. Structural: FAILED requires a typed pre-effect error code; everything else unproven is UNCERTAIN. No error-text matching anywhere.
D2. Durable intent before send; a command id is dispatched once, ever; UNCERTAIN leaves only through evidence. No automatic re-dispatch and no automatic replacement id exist anywhere in the tree.
The role files are the definitions, not the enforcement. The `tools` and `model` fields bind only whatever later reads them. See role-loadout-enforcement.
The credential-free tier (pure + isolated runtime) gates every re-pin and every merge through the harness CI job. No second suite may claim to verify the pin.

concerns.plannedOwner: a Command Governor policy layer over Prime's RLM child spawn (Gate P2/S5)
concerns.note: ADR 0008 invariant 6 has no enforcement point yet. Until a component owns this, harness/agents/*.md restrictions are documentation, and the conformance suite says so rather than implying otherwise.

concerns.plannedOwner: harness/extensions/cg-foreman (interface only in this revision; Gate S6)
concerns.note: Transport candidates are capability-gated and replaceable; the interface is fixed now so neither candidate's shape reaches the ledger. Explicitly out of scope for Issue #17.

concerns.plannedOwner: a Command Governor extension-owned durable sidecar next to the mutation ledger
concerns.note: Must not be the Prime session JSONL, and must not be confused with Prime's ack_result journal compaction, which is a receipt acknowledgement and not a foreman disposition.

concerns.plannedOwner: exactly one memory package, not yet chosen
concerns.note: Deferred deliberately. Prime resolves two session_before_compact handlers by load order with no error, so this must be exactly one owner forever.
Deferred. Memory is never authority for exact lifecycle, capability, safety or user-owned decision facts (ADR 0008 invariant 5).
ADR 0008 invariant 7 needs a single arbiter. Nothing in this revision gates tools.

concerns.plannedOwner: Prime's stable ACP v1 server, driven by the official SDK in a Gate S2 conformance harness
concerns.note: Out of scope for Issue #17 beyond one recorded fact: ACP mode leaves a resident worker after each invocation (Issue #15 D5), so the S2 harness must shut down and assert zero survivors, as the runtime fixture here already does.

concerns.plannedOwner: Gate S3 selection (Gondolin, container, or OpenShell)
concerns.note: Recorded requirement only: the daemon socket is a credential boundary (Issue #15 S0 finding 4); the environment-boundary owner above is the Governor-side half, OS containment is not chosen here.
